log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Scizor-Mega. Lead Archaludon+Grimmsnarl: priority Fake Out flinches the key support threat (Venusaur Sleep Powder or Raichu Fake Out denial) while Archaludon fires Electro Shot at Zard-Y for a possible OHKO that removes Drought. Backline Politoed switches in post-Mega to override sun with Drizzle, stripping Chlorophyll and weakening Fire for Scizor-Mega's priority Bullet Punch cleanup. Garganacl and Noivern benched: Garganacl underperformed g1, Noivern is outsped by sun Venusaur a
decisions.notebook:
Game 2 plan: lead Archaludon+Grimmsnarl, back Politoed+Scizor. Mega: Scizor-Mega.
Key damage verified: Archaludon Electro Shot vs Zard-Y = 68.6-156.9% (possible OHKO, 2x SE Electric vs Flying). Draco Meteor vs Venusaur = 46-100.6% NEUTRAL (Dragon is not SE vs Grass). Fake Out vs Venusaur = 8.6-19.4% (breaks Focus Sash). Combined Fake Out+Draco Meteor = 54.6-120% (likely but not guaranteed KO). Spirit Break vs Garchomp = 37.7-82% (2x SE, not OHKO). Electro Shot NVE 0.5x on Goodra-Hisui (Steel/Dragon); Archaludon has no SE move vs Goodra-Hisui.
Items restore between games in Bo3: Venusaur Focus Sash is intact for Game 2.
Politoed Drizzle only activates on entry; must switch in AFTER Zard-Y Mega Evolves to override Drought with rain. Rain removes Chlorophyll speed and weakens Fire 50%, protecting Scizor-Mega (4x Fire weak).
If opponent swaps Raichu for Talonflame: Gale Wings priority Brave Bird + Tailwind is the threat; Scizor-Mega Bullet Punch (+1) and rain-weakned Flare Blitz help, but speed control from Tailwind means I must disrupt Tailwind setup (Fake Out or KO Talonflame turn 1).
Goodra-Hisui SapSipper blocks Grass moves and is Steel/Dragon (same typing as Archaludon); Archaludon cannot hit it SE. If Goodra-Hisui is brought, switch to Scizor (Close Combat SE vs Steel) or Politoed (Hydro Pump neutral, Ice Beam neutral) and play around its low Speed (80-112).

decisions.rationale: Mega Charizard Y is the intended Mega. Charizard/Venusaur immediately turns the rain mode into a sun-speed and Solar Beam problem while retaining Sleep Powder disruption. Garchomp is the primary Archaludon answer; Raichu supplies Fake Out and Lightning Rod to deny or redirect Electro Shot. Heat Wave is a 4x threat into base Scizor, while Venusaur pressures Grimmsnarl with Sludge Bomb.

Fake Out Venusaur prevents the 48.5-114.1% Sludge Bomb OHKO on Grimmsnarl and breaks Focus Sash. Electro Shot threatens Charizard-Y for 62.2-109.8% (possible KO). If Charizard Protects, Electro Shot is wasted but Venusaur is flinched + Sash-broken — strong position for turn 2. If Charizard Heat Waves, Archaludon survives 31-70.9% then fires Electro Shot. Heat Wave to Grimmsnarl is only 0.5x (Dark resists Fire). Best risk-reward: neutralize Venusaur's Sash + dangerous Sludge Bomb while pressuring
decisions.notebook:
Game 2 plan: lead Archaludon+Grimmsnarl, back Politoed+Scizor. Mega: Scizor-Mega.
Key damage verified: Archaludon Electro Shot vs Zard-Y = 62.2-109.8% (possible OHKO, Expert Belt 2x SE). Heat Wave (Drought, spread) vs Archaludon = 31-70.9% (survivable). Sludge Bomb vs Grimmsnarl = 48.5-114.1% (possible OHKO — must prevent Venusaur from hitting Grimmsnarl). Draco Meteor vs Venusaur = 46-100.6% neutral (Dragon not SE vs Grass). Fake Out vs Venusaur = 8.6-19.4% (breaks Focus Sash).
Speed: Charizard-Y 132-167 > Archaludon 123 > Grimmsnarl 80. Venusaur Chlorophyll under Drought = 200-264 (outspeeds everything). Fake Out +3 priority always goes first.
Turn 2 plan if Charizard Protects: Electro Shot Charizard (no Protect available) or Draco Meteor Venusaur (no Sash, likely KO). If Charizard KO'd: Drought ends, Chlorophyll gone, Venusaur slow + Sash-broken — clean up with Scizor-Mega.
If opponent brings Talonflame: Gale Wings Brave Bird + Tailwind threat; use Fake Out or KO Talonflame turn 1.
If opponent brings Goodra-Hisui: SapSipper blocks Grass, Steel/Dragon same as Archaludon; switch to Scizor (Close Combat SE) or Politoed.
Politoed Drizzle must enter AFTER Zard-Y Mega Evolves to override Drought with rain. Rain weakens Fire 50%, protecting Scizor-Mega (4x Fire weak).

decisions.rationale: Mega Protect denies Archaludon’s immediate super-effective Electro Shot while Raichu enters safely: Lightning Rod can absorb an Electric attack aimed into its slot. This preserves Charizard Y and establishes sun plus Fake Out/Encore pressure for the next turn, without risking Venusaur being stopped by Grimmsnarl’s priority Fake Out.
decisions.notebook: Opponent led Archaludon/Grimmsnarl in G2, unlike its G1 rain-Steel mode. Respect Grimmsnarl priority disruption and Archaludon’s immediate Electric pressure on Charizard; Raichu is valuable as the Electric deterrent while Charizard Y supplies sun.

decisions.rationale: Charizard outspeeds both my Pokémon and Heat Wave can KO Grimmsnarl (35-115%) before any screen or Spirit Break goes up. Switching Grimmsnarl to Politoed (priority +6) guarantees Drizzle sets rain before moves resolve, halving Fire damage, forcing Solar Beam to charge, and disabling Chlorophyll. Archaludon's Electro Shot (SpA+1, Expert Belt, 2x SE) does 84-182% to Charizard — likely OHKO. If Charizard falls, rain persists, Venusaur stays slow, and Grimmsnarl is preserved at 100% for later use. P
decisions.notebook:
Game 2 plan: lead Archaludon+Grimmsnarl, back Politoed+Scizor. Mega: Scizor-Mega.
Key damage verified: Archaludon Electro Shot (SpA+1) vs Zard-Y = 84.3-181.7% (likely OHKO with Expert Belt 2x SE). Heat Wave (Drought, spread) vs Grimmsnarl = 35.1-114.7% (possible OHKO — Grimmsnarl must not stay in under Drought vs Zard-Y). Heat Wave (Drought, spread) vs Archaludon = 31-70.9% (survivable). Solar Beam vs Grimmsnarl = 26.2-85.9% (cannot OHKO alone). Thunderbolt vs Archaludon = 10.2-37.6% (negligible, 0.5x NVE). Draco Meteor vs Venusaur = 46-100.6% neutral.
Speed: Zard-Y 132-167 > Archaludon 123 > Grimmsnarl 80. Raichu 143-178 fastest active. Venusaur Chlorophyll under Drought = 200-264 (outspeeds everything); under rain = 100-132 (slow).
Turn 2: Switched Grimmsnarl to Politoed for Drizzle rain override. If Zard KO'd by Electro Shot, rain persists; bring Scizor-Mega safely (rain halves Fire, protecting 4x Fire weak). Politoed has Ice Beam (4x vs Garchomp), Hydro Pump, Helping Hand, Protect, Sitrus Berry.
Opponent tendencies: Led Zard+Venusaur, switched Venusaur to Raichu turn 1 (predicted Fake Out on Venusaur). Zard Protected turn 1 (wasted). Raichu took Fake Out (100%->73%).
If opponent brings Talonflame: Gale Wings Brave Bird + Tailwind threat; priority moves needed.
If opponent brings Goodra-Hisui: SapSipper blocks Grass; switch to Scizor (Close Combat SE) or use Politoed rain + Ice Beam neutral.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out moves before Prankster screens and denies Grimmsnarl’s disruption. Charizard is guaranteed faster than Archaludon and sun-boosted Flamethrower concentrates damage on the +1 Special Attack threat. Raichu’s Lightning Rod also makes an attempted Electro Shot into Charizard harmless, leaving Draco Meteor as Archaludon’s meaningful retaliation.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has shown an Archaludon/Grimmsnarl anti-sun lead in G2 rather than immediately using its rain mode. Prioritize denying Grimmsnarl’s priority screens while applying immediate pressure to boosted Archaludon; preserve Raichu when possible as the Electric redirection piece against Archaludon.

decisions.rationale: Raichu outspeeds Archaludon and Encore locks it into Electro Shot (redirected by Lightning Rod, useless). Switching Archaludon to Scizor nullifies Encore and brings in Scizor-Mega under rain (Fire weakness halved). Politoed Hydro Pump targets Zard-Y (2x SE + rain 1.5x = 71-154%, possible OHKO). Even if it misses, Zard-Y is weak under rain and Scizor-Mega + Politoed can handle next turn. Politoed survives any double-target (Thunderbolt 51-60% + Sitrus Berry).
decisions.notebook:
Game 2 plan: lead Archaludon+Grimmsnarl, back Politoed+Scizor. Mega: Scizor-Mega.
Key damage verified: Archaludon Electro Shot (SpA+1) vs Zard-Y = 84.3-181.7% (likely OHKO with Expert Belt 2x SE) BUT Lightning Rod redirects to Raichu (0.5x, useless). Draco Meteor (SpA+1) vs Zard-Y = 42.7-90.8% (neutral, cannot OHKO alone). Hydro Pump (rain) vs Zard-Y = 71.4-154.2% (possible OHKO). Draco Meteor + Hydro Pump combined = 114-245% (likely KO if both hit). Thunderbolt (+1 SpA Raichu) vs Politoed = 51-60.4% (survives with Sitrus Berry).
Speed: Raichu 143-178 > Zard-Y 132-167 > Archaludon 123 > Politoed 90 > Grimmsnarl 80. Raichu Encore outspeeds Archaludon, locking it into last move (Electro Shot). Switching Archaludon out is only reliable Encore counter.
Lightning Rod: Raichu immune to ALL Electric moves (even direct target) and gains +1 SpA each time. Electro Shot completely useless while Raichu active.
Rain (Drizzle Politoed) halves Fire damage and boosts Water 1.5x. Zard-Y Drought only activates on entry/switch, not while rain is active. Solar Beam takes 2 turns under rain.
Scizor-Mega under rain: 4x Fire weakness halved to 2x. Technician Bullet Punch (priority +1, 60 power) threatens Raichu. All Scizor moves NVE vs Zard-Y (Steel/Bug/Fighting all 0.5x vs Fire/Flying).
Opponent tendencies: Led Zard+Venusaur, switched Venusaur to Raichu turn 1 (predicted Fake Out). Zard Protected turn 1. Raichu took Fake Out (100%->73%). Turn 2: Raichu Fake Out on Politoed, Zard Flamethrower on Archaludon (63% HP, triggered Stamina +1 Def). Opponent uses Encore+Lightning Rod synergy deliberately

decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl slot a, Archaludon slot b. Grimmsnarl re-enters fresh so Fake Out (pri+3) is live — flinches Raichu before Encore resolves, protecting Archaludon. Archaludon at 63% with SpA+1 can Draco Meteor Zard-Y under rain for ~43-91%. Slot choice is minor in VGC targeting; this keeps a clean support-damage split.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: lost Scizor (Mega) and Politoed turns 1-3. Remaining: Archaludon 63% (SpA+1, Def+1, Expert Belt, last move Electro Shot — Encore bait), Grimmsnarl 100% (Light Clay, Prankster, Fake Out available on re-entry). Rain 4 turns left. Opponent: Zard-Y 100%, Raichu 73% (SpA+1, Lightning Rod, Encore available), Venusaur/Talonflame/Garchomp/Goodra-Hisui unseen. Key plan: Fake Out Raichu to prevent Encore, Draco Meteor Zard-Y. Watch for Raichu Protect predicting Fake Out. Series score 1-0 in my favor; need to close game 2.

decisions.rationale: Raichu is guaranteed faster than Politoed and boosted Thunderbolt is the immediate Politoed KO, removing rain pressure before Hydro Pump. Flamethrower is the accurate single-target pressure into Archaludon; Lightning Rod continues to deny its Electro Shot against Charizard.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s G2 anti-sun mode showed Archaludon/Grimmsnarl lead, then pivoted Politoed to establish rain. Archaludon has Expert Belt, Stamina, Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, Protect; Grimmsnarl has Prankster screens/Fake Out. Preserve Lightning Rod when feasible to deny Archaludon Electric pressure into Charizard.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out (+3 pri) flinches Raichu before Encore. Draco Meteor does 59-139% to Raichu; with Fake Out chip (12-30%), near-certain KO at 73%. Removing Raichu eliminates both Encore lock and Lightning Rod, freeing Electro Shot for Zard next turn. If Raichu Protects, both moves whiff but Zard's rain-nerfed Heat Wave maxes at 43.6% on Archaludon (survives at ~19%). No switch available so Encore is permanent — must remove Raichu now.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: lost Scizor+Politoed. Remaining: Archaludon 63% (SpA+1, Def+1, Expert Belt, Modest, Electro Shot last=Encore bait), Grimmsnarl 100% (Light Clay, Prankster, Careful). Rain 3 turns. Opponent: Zard-Y 100% (Timid, Drought overridden by rain, Fire moves weakened), Raichu 73% (SpA+1, Lightning Rod, Encore available, Timid, Sitrus). Venusaur/Talonflame/Garchomp/Goodra-Hisui unseen. Series 1-0 my favor. Key: Raichu Encore is permanent lock since no switch available. Must KO Raichu or prevent Encore. Rain makes Zard-Y nearly harmless (Heat Wave 13-44% on Archaludon). After Raichu down, Electro Shot hits Zard-Y SE without Lightning Rod redirect.

decisions.rationale: Flamethrower pressures Grimmsnarl immediately while Encore punishes its most valuable line: a Prankster screen. Lightning Rod continues to deny Electro Shot into Charizard, so Archaludon cannot exploit rain’s remaining turns for meaningful Electric pressure. If Grimmsnarl screens, it is locked; if it attacks, Charizard gets clean chip and Encore constrains its next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent G2 anti-sun mode showed Archaludon/Grimmsnarl lead, then Politoed rain. Archaludon: Expert Belt, Stamina, Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, Protect. Grimmsnarl: Light Clay, Prankster, Fake Out, Reflect, Light Screen, Spirit Break. Preserve Lightning Rod when feasible to deny Archaludon Electric pressure into Charizard; punish Prankster screens with Encore where possible.

decisions.rationale: Switch to Garchomp. It is faster than both foes, is Ground-typed against Archaludon’s Electric pressure, and threatens the Steel/Dragon with Life Orb Stomping Tantrum. Venusaur’s strongest listed Grass move is heavily resisted by Archaludon and it is vulnerable to Flash Cannon.

Garchomp outspeeds and can OHKO 63% Archaludon with SE Stomping Tantrum (40-118%). Prankster Reflect goes first, halving all physical damage for 8 turns (Light Clay). Archaludon Protects to dodge the KO. Next turn with Reflect up, Archaludon safely Electro Shots Charizard (SE, boosts SpA from -2 to -1) while rain persists. Grimmsnarl tanks rain-weakened Fire easily.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Archaludon 63% SpA-2 (Expert Belt, Modest, Stamina Def+1), Grimmsnarl 77% (Light Clay, Prankster, Careful). Fainted: Politoed, Scizor. Opp: Zard-Y 100% (Timid, Drought overridden by rain), Garchomp 100% (Jolly, Life Orb, Rough Skin), Venusaur 100% (Modest, Focus Sash, Chlorophyll - slow in rain). Raichu fainted. Rain 2 turns. Plan: Reflect+Protect T5, then Electro Shot Zard-Y T6 to start SpA recovery. Garchomp is primary threat; Spirit Break SE chip later. Venusaur Sash must be broken before KO. Series 1-0.

decisions.rationale: Both attackers are faster at normal priority and threaten their respective foes immediately. Flamethrower pressures the screen setter while Life Orb STAB Stomping Tantrum is super effective into Archaludon. Light Screen plus Protect is their strongest stall line, but direct split pressure still gives the best chance to remove one foe now and preserves Venusaur for the endgame.

Focus-fire Garchomp with both SE moves. Garchomp outspeeds but Reflect halves Stomping Tantrum's physical damage, giving Archaludon ~50% survival odds at 63% HP. If Archaludon survives, Draco Meteor (36-118% at SpA-2+Expert Belt) + Spirit Break (31-102%) combined almost certainly KO Garchomp. If Garchomp Protects, we lose tempo but opponent also wastes a turn in rain where Zard-Y's Fire is weak. Removing Garchomp is critical — it's the only Ground STAB threat to Archaludon. Even at SpA-4 post-Dr
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Opp leads Zard-Y+Venusaur, brings Garchomp+Raichu. Raichu fainted T4 (Lightning Rod redirected Electro Shot T2). Zard-Y Timid, Drought overridden by Politoed Drizzle rain. Garchomp Jolly Life Orb Rough Skin. Venusaur Modest Focus Sash Chlorophyll (slow in rain, no sun when rain ends since Drought doesn't reactivate). Opp plays aggressively, double-targets for KOs. Series 1-0. Key: Stomping Tantrum doubles BP (150) when previous move failed/blocked. Reflect halves physical only, not special. Archaludon Expert Belt boosts SE 1.2x. When rain ends T7, weather is clear (Drought already activated on Mega Evo, won't reactivate). Venusaur speed 100-132 without Chlorophyll in clear weather.

decisions.rationale: Apply immediate split pressure while both attackers are faster. Flamethrower continues forcing Grimmsnarl down, while Stomping Tantrum heavily pressures Archaludon despite Reflect. If Grimmsnarl uses Fake Out on one slot, the other still advances the board; Archaludon’s repeat Protect has reduced success.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Archaludon)
decisions.rationale: Light Screen via Prankster (+1 priority) is guaranteed before any foe move. Archaludon Protects to survive at 8%. Spirit Break lacks Prankster (physical) so Grimmsnarl at 80 Spe likely dies before acting. Game is near-lost but this extends the turn and preserves the only sliver of hope if the opponent misplay or miss.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 essentially lost (both mons near death, Archaludon -4 SpA). For Game 3: Opp brings Zard-Y+Venusaur+Garchomp+Raichu. Raichu Lightning Rod redirects Electric moves (Electro Shot wasted T2). Venusaur Focus Sash Chlorophyll slow without sun (Drought only on Mega Evo, doesn't reactivate). Garchomp Jolly LO Rough Skin with Stomping Tantrum (150 BP if prev move blocked). Opp plays aggressively, double-targets for KOs. My team: Archaludon Expert Belt Stamina, Grimmsnarl Light Clay Prankster, Politoed Sitrus Drizzle, Scizor Scizorite Technician. Consider: lead to avoid Raichu redirecting Electro Shot; Politoed rain overrides Drought; Scizor-Mega slow (75 base) but Technician Bullet Punch priority; Reflect halves physical only. Stomping Tantrum doubles when prev move fails/blocked — don't Protect predictably into Garchomp.

decisions.rationale: Charizard is guaranteed faster and Flamethrower cleanly removes the immediate Archaludon threat without Heat Wave accuracy or spread reduction. If Grimmsnarl Fake Outs Venusaur, Archaludon is still gone and Charizard can finish Grimmsnarl next turn. If Archaludon Protects, Sludge Bomb removes Grimmsnarl unless it uses Fake Out; either line leaves its heavily reduced Special Attack pressure manageable.

Game 2 is lost: Archaludon at 8% with -4 SpA faces two healthy foes. Flamethrower KOs through Light Screen regardless. Electro Shot on Charizard is the best chip option (2x SE + Expert Belt) even at -4 SpA, doing more meaningful damage than Draco Meteor on Sash Venusaur. Protect has reduced odds and no path to victory. Accept the loss and prepare for Game 3.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 plan: Opp likely brings Zard-Y+Venusaur+Garchomp+Raichu again. Key counters: Politoed Drizzle overrides Drought (Zard-Y needs Mega turn to get sun, rain cuts Fire damage); Scizor-Mega Technician Bullet Punch priority KOs Raichu and chips Venusaur/Charizard; lead Politoed+Scizor to set rain and threaten Raichu with BP before Lightning Rod matters. Avoid Electro Shot when Raichu is alive (Lightning Rod redirects). Don't Protect predictably into Garchomp (Stomping Tantrum 150 BP). Grimmsnarl screens + Spirit Break for SpA control. Archaludon Expert Belt Stamina best saved for late-game cleanup under rain. Opp double-targets aggressively for KOs.

decisions.rationale: Charizard is faster and Flamethrower is a guaranteed KO on the revealed low-HP Archaludon even through its Steel/Dragon typing. Venusaur Protect avoids any needless exposure; Archaludon’s reduced-success Protect is its only meaningful escape line.

reflections.summary: Archaludon was forced to use Draco Meteor twice (KOing Raichu and Garchomp), dropping its SpA to -4 and leaving it unable to threaten Charizard+Venusaur late. Scizor-Mega and Politoed fell early (turns 1-3) despite the rain plan, and sun-boosted Charizard Flamethrower plus Chlorophyll Venusaur (Focus Sash) cleaned up the weakened remaining core. The team-preview plan of leading Politoed+Scizor to set rain and pressure Raichu failed because Scizor's 4x Fire weakness is too fragile even under rain
reflections.adjustment: Lead Grimmsnarl+Politoed to guarantee screens+rain before committing Scizor-Mega. Preserve Archaludon's SpA by using Flash Cannon or Electro Shot instead of double Draco Meteor—save Draco for a single critical KO. Prioritize eliminating Venusaur early (Focus Sash + Chlorophyll under sun is the opponent's real win condition); consider Scizor Bullet Punch to break the sash then finish with another attacker.
reflections.notebook: Opp Game 2 brought: Zard-Y, Venusaur, Garchomp, Raichu (same as predicted). Venusaur = Focus Sash + Chlorophyll; under sun it outspeeds entire team and is the real wincon. Charizard-Y spams Flamethrower after Mega Evolving turn 1 for Drought. Garchomp uses Stomping Tantrum (150 BP if previous move failed). Raichu = Fake Out + Lightning Rod support. Opp double-targets aggressively for KOs. Key lesson: Scizor-Mega 4x Fire weak is too fragile even under rain—needs screens support before switching in. Archaludon must avoid double Draco Meteor or it becomes useless late. Game 3 plan: Lead Grimmsnarl+Politoed for guaranteed screens+rain; break Venusaur Focus Sash with priority before it sets up under sun; save Archaludon for late cleanup with intact SpA; use Draco Meteor at most once.

reflections.summary: Won because Garchomp put Archaludon into cleanup range while Charizard and Venusaur removed Grimmsnarl and finished through its screens. Mega Charizard Y was still a suitable win condition, but the Raichu lead was vulnerable to Grimmsnarl Fake Out plus Archaludon Draco Meteor.
reflections.adjustment: Against the Grimmsnarl/Archaludon mode, lead Garchomp beside Charizard rather than Raichu beside Charizard to apply immediate Archaludon pressure; keep Mega Y, but do not rely on Raichu remaining alive to contain it.
reflections.notebook: Archaludon will use Draco Meteor to remove Raichu rather than solely pursuing Electric pressure; Lightning Rod is not a dependable long-term answer. Opponent can establish both Light Clay screens even while Archaludon protects. Future plan: prioritize immediate Archaludon pressure with Garchomp/Charizard and preserve Venusaur to break Grimmsnarl or close after screens.
